section_summary: This section follows American President Lines’ efforts to transfer yen earnings from Japan in 1939. Company letters, balance schedules, Embassy telegrams, and State Department memoranda document delayed exchange permits, claims of unequal treatment, and a Japanese proposal to issue monthly permits with a two-month lag. It also contains Japanese exchange-control rules and several Philippine newspaper clippings on regional political and economic affairs.

subfiles.title: McAdoo letter on blocked yen revenues
subfiles.from: William G. McAdoo, American President Lines
subfiles.about: Requests U.S. intervention to secure timely conversion and transfer of the company’s yen earnings.
subfiles.summary: The company says delayed permits have blocked substantial working capital, exposed it to yen depreciation, and impaired competition with Japanese and other foreign shipping. It disputes Japanese complaints about its business practices, while acknowledging that it pays crew advances in dollars. McAdoo asks the Department to obtain permits for April through June receipts and regular monthly approvals thereafter.

subfiles.title: Schedule A: Yen position at July 7, 1939
subfiles.from: Arthur B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.about: Tabulates receipts, permitted conversions, and yen still lacking exchange permits.
subfiles.summary: The schedule reports ¥658,776.36 without permits at July 7.

subfiles.title: Exhibit 1: Crew advance instructions
subfiles.about: Limits the timing of U.S. currency advances to crews before Japanese and Italian port calls.
subfiles.summary: Dollar advances for Yokohama, Kobe, or Naples require departure from the preceding port and proximity to arrival.

subfiles.title: Japan to help P.I. celebrate
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese broadcast and Philippine events for the Commonwealth anniversary.
subfiles.summary: A Tokyo goodwill broadcast is planned alongside parades, speeches, and celebrations across the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Yoshida has good record
subfiles.about: Profiles incoming Japanese consul general Tanichiro Yoshida.
subfiles.summary: The article recounts Yoshida’s consular and Foreign Office postings before his assignment to the Philippines.

subfiles.title: China consul lauds Quezon
subfiles.about: Reports the Chinese consul’s response to Quezon’s remarks on retail trade and property rights.
subfiles.summary: Kwangson Young praises assurances that foreign merchants’ established rights and investments will be respected.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner may visit China and Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Sayre’s travel plans and review of Philippine economic measures.
subfiles.summary: Sayre discusses price controls, retail trade, the reserve bank law, neutrality, and possible travel in Asia.

subfiles.title: P.I. fishing dominated by Nippons
subfiles.about: Reports Aquino’s claim that Japanese interests control many Philippine fishing boats.
subfiles.summary: Aquino calls for stronger fisheries enforcement and training; a fish warden reports apparent customs violations.

subfiles.title: McAdoo inquiry on July 12 letter
subfiles.about: Requests a telegraphic response concerning the yen matter raised in his July 12 letter.
subfiles.summary: McAdoo asks Hull to telegraph about his earlier appeal.

subfiles.title: Instruction to press Japan for an answer
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to stress U.S. concern and seek an approximate reply date.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is told to press the Japanese foreign minister on the shipping-revenue transfer issue.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to McAdoo
subfiles.about: Updates McAdoo on instructions sent to the Tokyo Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it seeks a system for prompt, regular transfer of company revenues.

subfiles.title: Hull reply to McAdoo
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s financial difficulties and describes U.S. representations to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull says the Department has asked Japan to establish regular transfers and will seek a date for its reply.

subfiles.title: Correction to yen schedule
subfiles.about: Corrects currency labels in Schedule A attached to the July 12 letter.
subfiles.summary: Two first-column dollar signs were erroneous; every figure in that schedule is yen.

subfiles.title: Despatch 4005: Changes in Japanese foreign exchange control law
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Explains Japan’s June 1939 amendments to its exchange-control rules.
subfiles.summary: The despatch describes a ¥500 limit on travelers’ export of money and a ¥200 limit on importing currency without permission. It links the import rule to purchases of cheap yen abroad and encloses a translation of the ordinance.

subfiles.title: Translation of Ministry of Finance Ordinance No. 27
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Finance; translated by the American Embassy
subfiles.about: Sets out amendments to Japanese rules for travel funds and imported banknotes.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance reduces permitted travel funds to ¥500, generally requires permission to import more than ¥200 in Japanese notes, and requires import reports. It takes effect July 1.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on April and May permits
subfiles.about: Reports progress on American President Lines’ blocked receipts.
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports an April permit and an expected May permit, and asks whether the funds can be described as U.S. Government funds.

subfiles.title: Department instruction on shipping remittances
subfiles.about: Directs stronger representations for regular transfer of American shipping earnings.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks the Embassy to approach the foreign minister and seek a reply date. It supplies arguments based on the treatment of foreign-flag shipping and says the position covers all American shipping companies regardless of ownership.

subfiles.title: McAdoo thanks Hull for intervention
subfiles.about: Reports a yen collection and an expected May permit.
subfiles.summary: McAdoo thanks Hull, reports collection of ¥270,773.65, and expects May permits in early August.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 380 on diplomatic approaches
subfiles.about: Details Embassy pressure for a continuing remittance arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Dooman recounts approaches to Yoshizawa, the vice minister, and the Foreign Office. He says Japanese officials are exploring a way to transfer the company’s funds promptly and that he requested a date for a favorable reply.

subfiles.title: Adviser’s memorandum on arguments for shipping transfers
subfiles.about: Evaluates arguments for seeking preferentially prompt transfers of American shipping earnings.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum questions whether the company’s financial need and the contrast with Japanese lines establish discrimination by Japan. It distinguishes prompt permits from exemption from exchange control and cautions against relying on reciprocity. It proposes an argument based on national treatment of foreign-flag shipping; pages 442–443 appear out of textual order in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Maritime Commission counsel
subfiles.about: Records discussion of a possible Shipping Act response to blocked yen earnings.
subfiles.summary: Frank B. Goertner identifies Section 26 of the Shipping Act of 1916 as a possible basis for investigation and publicity if Japan refuses regular remittances.

subfiles.title: Shipping Act of 1916, Section 26
subfiles.about: Sets out authority to investigate unequal treatment of U.S. vessels abroad.
subfiles.summary: The provision authorizes investigation, diplomatic action, and, if needed, a presidential report to Congress.

subfiles.title: Confidential forwarding letter to Tokyo
subfiles.to: American chargé d’affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards the July 24 conversation memorandum for confidential information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Goertner conversation memorandum concerning American President Lines’ blocked yen.

subfiles.title: Poole letter forwarding Steen’s account
subfiles.about: Supplies evidence concerning possible preferential Japanese treatment of French shipping.
subfiles.summary: Poole encloses Steen’s letter, requests confidentiality for its source, and promises weekly yen-position reports.

subfiles.title: Steen report on foreign-line remittance permits
subfiles.about: Reports information that a French line received faster Japanese exchange permits.
subfiles.summary: Steen relays MacDonald’s confidential account of a French trade agreement and favorable permits; reports on German and Italian lines remain less certain.

subfiles.title: Yen position at July 28, 1939
subfiles.about: States the company’s remaining yen and dollar equivalent in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥512,889.93 in Japan, including ¥450,933.84 without permits.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission letter on French permits
subfiles.about: Passes on reports of favorable Japanese remittance terms for French shipping interests.
subfiles.summary: Land reports a possible French agreement benefiting Messageries Maritimes and less specific reports about German and Italian lines.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Admiral Land
subfiles.about: Acknowledges evidence on French permits and updates Land on negotiations.
subfiles.summary: The Department says the Embassy continues to press for regular transfers and that a May permit has been approved.

subfiles.title: Welles update to Admiral Land
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s proposed regular permit schedule.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says monthly permits will be issued regularly with a two-month lag and promises a formal note.

subfiles.title: Yen position at August 4, 1939
subfiles.about: Lists receipts still awaiting exchange permits.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥497,933.84 in Japan, with no permits for the listed receipts.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on May permit approval
subfiles.about: Reports further pressure for a reply and issuance of May permits.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is assured that the May permit has been approved and will be issued shortly.

subfiles.title: Ballantine update to American President Lines
subfiles.about: Informs the company of Japan’s planned monthly permit system.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine reports regular permits with a two-month lag, pending formal confirmation.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on issued May permits
subfiles.about: Confirms issuance of permits for May receipts.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office says May permits were issued and promises an answer on automatic monthly remittances.

subfiles.title: Department update to McAdoo on May receipts
subfiles.about: Reports issuance of May remittance permits and an expected answer on regular transfers.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine relays Embassy news of May permits and an imminent Japanese response on a continuing system.

subfiles.title: Poole update on May exchange permit
subfiles.about: Relays company reports that the May permit awaits final signature.
subfiles.summary: Poole quotes Yokohama and Shanghai reports and expects completion shortly.

subfiles.title: Land letter on May receipts remitted
subfiles.about: Thanks the Department and reports transfer of May receipts.
subfiles.summary: Land says the full May receipts, about $41,500, were being remitted from Yokohama and Kobe.

subfiles.title: Yen position at August 11, 1939
subfiles.about: States the company’s unpermitted yen receipts as of August 11.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥528,933.84 in Japan and no permits for the listed receipts.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on regular future permits
subfiles.about: Reports an informal Japanese commitment to regular monthly permits.
subfiles.summary: Permits are promised with a two-month lag, starting with June receipts in September; a formal note is expected.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs file note on exchange-control revisions
subfiles.about: Links a later Tokyo despatch to the earlier report on Japanese exchange-control changes.
subfiles.summary: Notes that despatch 4049 encloses Foreign Office explanations of revisions covered in despatch 4005.

subfiles.title: Despatch 4049: Changes in Japanese foreign exchange control law
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Japanese Foreign Office explanations of exchange-control revisions.
subfiles.summary: Dooman encloses translations of a note verbale and summary, and says copies were circulated to U.S. consulates for American citizens.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office note verbale on exchange-control rules
subfiles.about: Forwards a summary and highlights reporting and permit requirements for currency carried abroad.
subfiles.summary: The note calls for customs reports and mentions permits for certain ¥100 notes even within the ¥500 allowance.

subfiles.title: Summary of revised foreign exchange-control ordinance
subfiles.about: Summarizes travel-money limits and imported-banknote reporting duties.
subfiles.summary: Travelers may carry up to ¥500 without a special permit; importing over ¥200 in Japanese notes requires permission. Banknote imports must be reported at entry or, for other channels, within two weeks.

subfiles.title: Poole letter forwarding comparative shipping reports
subfiles.about: Sends Yokohama reports about permits granted to other foreign shipping lines.
subfiles.summary: Poole says Messageries Maritimes shows the clearest apparent advantage and encloses an August 18 yen report.

subfiles.title: Yen position at August 18, 1939
subfiles.about: Reports yen receipts still awaiting permits and an Embassy effort to secure future policy.
subfiles.summary: Lists ¥393,931.13 in Japan without permits, worth about $107,300.

subfiles.title: MacDonald report on German and Italian lines
subfiles.about: Compares remittance permits for German and Italian shipping lines.
subfiles.summary: MacDonald describes Norddeutscher Lloyd’s four-month spread and reports limited information on Lloyd Triestino and Hamburg America Line.

subfiles.title: Spengler report on foreign shipping permits
subfiles.about: Compares exchange permits obtained by several foreign shipping lines.
subfiles.summary: Spengler reports Messageries Maritimes permits through June, while other foreign lines generally had permits only through March or earlier.

subfiles.title: McAdoo telegram protesting the two-month lag
subfiles.about: Requests renewed representations for faster payment of June and July receipts.
subfiles.summary: McAdoo calls the proposed schedule unfair and asks for prompt payment of roughly $110,000.

subfiles.title: Hull reply on further representations
subfiles.about: Explains why the Department will await stronger evidence before another approach to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges the delays but says regular permits were secured after repeated representations. Without conclusive evidence that the company receives worse treatment than other lines, he sees no useful purpose in another approach at present.

subfiles.title: Poole letter forwarding Matteson’s Kobe report
subfiles.about: Encloses further information on exchange permits issued to foreign steamship lines.
subfiles.summary: Poole forwards Matteson’s July 26 Kobe letter and notes that it covers additional foreign lines.
